author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔐 $11M Cork Protocol Hack Exposed Critical Uniswap V4 Hook Flaws

On May 28, 2025, Cork Protocol lost $11M due to missing access control in their Uniswap V4 hook contract. The attacker exploited poorly protected beforeSwap calls, tricking the protocol into crediting fake token deposits.

Key issues:
- No restriction on who could call hook functions
- Allowed cross-market token confusion (using insurance tokens as safe tokens)
- No pool validation or whitelisting
- Token states overlapped across markets (Singleton pattern)

Despite multiple audits, this vulnerability slipped through, showing the complexity of Uniswap V4 hooks security.

Takeaway:  
Always enforce strict onlyPoolManager access and validate tokens and pools carefully when building hooks on Uniswap V4.

🛡️ Critical AMM Bug Allows Hidden Rug Pull via Duplicate Pool Creation

A gas-optimized AMM called ZAMM lets attackers create the same coin/pool pair multiple times in one second, hiding LP tokens to later rug the pool. 

This happens because pool IDs depend only on user address + timestamp, with no reads to detect overwrites—letting attackers steal funds unnoticed.

Regular pools are safe; only AMM-created coins are vulnerable.

Quick fix: ZAMM hid duplicates in UI and added docs.

🛠️ Prevention: Use a global nonce or check existing pools before creation.

Detect via fuzzing and supply ≤ balance checks—unit tests often miss this.

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔐 EVM Calldata Decoded: Essential for DeFi Security  

Understanding raw calldata—the encoded inputs sent to Ethereum smart contracts—is key to decoding transactions and spotting anomalies.  

- Calldata consists of static (fixed size) and dynamic (variable size) parameters.  
- The first 4 bytes identify the function selector, guiding the EVM which function to run.  
- Dynamic types start with an offset + length, followed by their data.  
Mastering this lets you audit, debug, and build safer contracts.  

Read full guide 👉 here

🚀 Solidity Precision Tip

In Solidity, always multiply before dividing to keep full precision. 

• Using 1e18 simulates decimals since Solidity has no real decimals.  
• This makes 100% equal to 1e18.  
• For example, 25% is represented as 2.5e17.  

Follow this to avoid precision loss in calculations.

🚨 Wormhole Bridge $320M Hack Explained

On Feb 2, 2022, Wormhole Bridge on Solana suffered a massive hack due to a smart contract vulnerability, losing ~120,000 wETH (~$320M).  

The attacker exploited a weak verify_signatures function by injecting a fake sysvar account, bypassing security to mint unauthorized wETH.  

• Initial fees came from Tornado Cash, hiding attack origins  
• Stolen assets crossed from Solana to Ethereum, then swapped for USDC and SOL  
• The attacker still holds over $297M in crypto today  

This case highlights how deprecated functions and poor sysvar validation create critical risks in cross-chain bridges.  

Always audit your smart contracts with trusted experts to prevent such breaches.

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 BNB Bridge Hack Explained

In Oct 2022, the BNB Bridge was hacked due to a flaw in its Merkle proof verification. The bug arose because path nodes could have both Left and Right flags set, allowing attackers to inject malicious transfers. 

• The bridge only kept one root hash on-chain, relying on user-controlled data for proofs.  
• The vulnerability let attackers bypass verification by exploiting inconsistent hash calculations.  
• Fixes required aligning side checks for root and subsequent leaf proofs.  
• No library patch was made; BNB Chain fixed nodes instead.  

This hack highlights the risks of gas optimization and the importance of consistent verification in Web3 security.

🛡️ Cross-Chain NFT Sync Glitch Exposed

  In a recent audit for Yuga Labs, a risky edge case in their lzRead integration was uncovered.  
  This bug could silently freeze NFT syncing across all chains using LayerZero v2.  

• lzRead relies on DVNs to verify on-chain reads; if a read reverts, verification fails.  
• Failed verification causes message blocking and stalls the entire cross-chain pipeline.  
• The issue arose from a function that reverted when NFTs were locked, halting syncing indefinitely.  
• Recommended fix: return structured data instead of reverting to keep DVNs verifying smoothly.  
• Yuga Labs applied the fix prior to launch, showcasing the need for protocol-aware audits.  

This case highlights the complexity of cross-chain messaging and importance of deep integration testing.

🔐 Zero-Knowledge Proofs in Real Life: Privacy Beyond Blockchain

👑 Dangers of Transferring Lamports in Solana

Transferring lamports to arbitrary accounts can cause program failures due to hidden restrictions: accounts must remain rent-exempt, not be executable, or reserved.  

Even if an account is marked writable, it can be automatically downgraded to read-only, which will block operations and render the contract nonfunctional.  

It is better to avoid direct transfers, storing returns in a PDA storage instead to protect against unpredictable changes and bugs.  

These nuances have already caused real problems in DeFi and require careful attention when developing secure Solana smart contracts.

🛡️ Cyclic Groups and the Discrete Logarithm in Cryptography

A cyclic group is a set of elements generated by repeatedly applying an operation to a single element — the generator.  

The security of many protocols is based on the discrete logarithm problem — finding the exponent of the generator that produces a given element, which is considered a computationally hard problem.  

Using subgroups of prime order enhances the security and efficiency of cryptography and zero-knowledge proofs, allowing secret values to be hidden without revealing the information itself.  

Cryptography relies on the hardness of solving the discrete logarithm problem in cyclic groups, which ensures the protection of private keys and the anonymity of data.

🛡️ Critical Vulnerability in Permit2: Irreversible DoS Griefing

The SignatureVerification::verify function calls claimedSigner::isValidSignature for contracts, which is generally safe. However, if a contract uses Permit2 with permitWitnessTransferFrom and generates its transaction ID based on non-substitutable data, an attacker can harm all users.

The attacker creates a contract with a signature that is always valid, changes the amount to 1 wei, and substitutes the user address. This causes a DoS where honest transactions keep reverting while the attacker’s costs remain minimal.

🧩 Homomorphisms — the foundation of zero-knowledge

A homomorphism is a function that preserves the structure of mathematical operations when transitioning from secret data to its encrypted form or commitments.

This allows performing computations on hidden data without revealing it, which is critical for zero-knowledge proofs.

In protocols like PLONK, operations on commitments mirror operations on the original values, maintaining confidentiality and integrity.

This way, complex computations can be proven through simple checks without disclosing the data itself.

🌉 Polygon Security: Risks of PoS and zkEVM

Polygon combines a PoS sidechain with zkEVM, but each layer has its own risks.

The PoS bridge is vulnerable due to centralized validators and insufficient protection at the Ethereum layer.

zkEVM provides reliable proofs but is still centralized and controlled by the Council, with fast upgrades executed without a timelock.

Errors in zk-chains can lead to incorrect state transitions, which is an important consideration for developers.

Polygon’s hybrid architecture requires special attention to bridges, validators, and governance to reduce systemic risks.

🐍 Solana Security Basics: From EVM to SVM

Solana stores data in Program Derived Addresses (PDAs) — separate accounts with strict access controls that are crucial for security.

Cross-Program Invocation (CPI) allows programs to interact but requires verification of the correctness of PDA signatures.

SPL tokens differ from ERC-20 — balances are stored in separate Token Accounts, which affects management and security.

Transactions on Solana are atomic and size-limited, protecting against partial failures and attacks.

SOL gives programs access to the entire account balance, so control and restrictions are critical to prevent losses.

Coordinated upgrade management and transparent infrastructure are critical for maintaining trust and stability.

🛡 Oracle and Pricing Risks in Smart Contracts

Using oracles and price feeds in DeFi often leads to vulnerabilities such as price manipulation via flash loans, liquidity issues, and front-running.

The most common mistakes are relying on the spot price, lacking timing protection, and improper data aggregation. All of these open the door to attacks and losses.

It is important to consider update delays, mathematical or parameter defects, and to avoid hardcoded price assumptions.

For complex oracles, it is better to use multiple sources and median values to make manipulation more difficult.

🛡️ TON Security: Key Features and Risks

TON is a unique blockchain with an asynchronous smart contract execution model, which eliminates classic reentrancy vulnerabilities.

Data is stored in cells — a structure with size limitations, simplifying logic and enhancing security.

However, due to the asynchronous nature, it is important to properly handle bounced messages; otherwise, loss of control over the state and vulnerabilities may occur.

There are no EOA (Externally Owned Account) addresses in TON — all accounts are contracts, so address validation and wallet code verification are critically important for asset protection.

Overflow, division by zero, and data serialization errors are still relevant and require careful attention.

Audits provide a targeted assessment of current security, but they become outdated and require updates to protect against new threats.

🥪 Sandwich Attacks in DEXs

Sandwich attacks occur when an attacker places two transactions around your pending transaction, manipulating the price and capturing your profit.

The main cause is the lack of slippage protection, which allows your trade to execute at a worse price.

Adding a parameter for the minimum acceptable output amount in the swap function blocks these attacks — if the price changes too much, the transaction is automatically reverted.

Thus, simple slippage protection reduces vulnerability to mempool manipulation.

🔐 Soundness Errors in ZK Schemes and Their Risks

ZK schemes require precise constraints on computations; otherwise, an attacker can prove false statements.

A common issue is insufficient binding of computed values to public outputs, which gives the attacker freedom to manipulate.

It is also important to explicitly define the semantics of integer operations and ranges, otherwise proofs can be forged.

Real-world cases like zkSync Era and Kakarot demonstrate the consequences of such errors — the ability to modify critical data without breaking the proof.

Overall, any missing check is a potential vulnerability that allows forging proofs.

🛡️ Proper use of require in DeFi for protocol security

Instead of checking conditions only inside functions, it’s worth applying the FREI-PI approach, which combines function checks and key protocol invariants.

This helps protect DeFi protocols from errors that violate the main security rules, for example, preventing a state with an unsafe lending position.

The classic Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern is useful but too local and does not guarantee the preservation of the core protocol invariant.

FREI-PI allows all operations to be done within a single transaction while maintaining the security of the entire protocol.

⚙️ Fusaka Update: Important Ethereum Security Changes

Fusaka introduces a gas limit per transaction — a maximum of about 16.78 million gas, which may cause failures for "heavy" smart contracts. 

The limits and costs of the MODEXP operations have been changed, affecting gas usage and potentially causing errors when gas is fixed.

A new opcode CLZ has been added for optimization, but it may cause issues on L2 and has a special case when the input is 0.

A precompile P256VERIFY has been added for verifying signatures on secp256r1, important for cross-platform security.

Paying attention to these updates will help avoid failures and maintain smart contract security.

We have identified 5 serious blind spots in the Base protocols: sequencer censorship without fallback, lack of fraud proofs, outdated cross-chain callbacks, vulnerable paymasters, and double-spending risks on the bridge.

Each problem has proven solutions: fallback to L1, fraud-proof safeguards, strict nonces and timelocks, operation limits, and atomic bridge calls.

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🤖 Solidity Auditor v3 Released Open Source

Solidity Auditor v3 is now available as a free and open-source AI security tool, with performance reportedly matching top-ranked security contest results from a year ago.

The tool is already being used by thousands of Solidity developers to review smart contract security.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔍 $39.5M in Exolix Swap History Exposed via Broken API

Partner JWTs found in public repos and decompiled APKs gave full read access to 355,944 swap records — deposit addresses, withdrawal addresses, on-chain hashes, and amounts.

9 of the top 11 pairs involve Monero, directly linking privacy coin users to transparent-chain addresses. Exolix called it a feature.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
⚠️ Logic Flaw Could Have Drained DeFi Vault

A security review of RetoSwap uncovered a logic flaw that allowed any user to assign themselves as an Arbiter and gain withdrawal privileges.

The issue could have led to a full vault drain and was fixed with access controls and withdrawal address restrictions.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 BY Token Exploited on BNB Chain

A suspicious attack targeting BY Token on BNB Chain resulted in estimated losses of approximately $88.4K.

The incident was detected by TenArmor, which flagged the exploit transaction shortly after the attack.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Critical Zcash Bug Could Mint Unlimited ZEC

Zcash disclosed a critical vulnerability that could have enabled attackers to mint unlimited koi counterfeit ZEC.

The issue remained exploitable for approximately 4 years before being patched. It is not known whether the vulnerability was ever exploited.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
⚠️ Crypto Neobank Attack Surfaces Extend Beyond Smart Contracts

Crypto neobanks combine traditional banking and crypto infrastructure, creating security risks across multiple layers including custody, card issuing, KYC, mobile applications, and on-chain settlement.

The $49.5M Infini exploit highlighted how operational security failures, such as an unrevoked admin key, can bypass audited smart contracts entirely.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🤖 AI May Strengthen DeFi Security, Not Just Attackers

Concerns are growing that increasingly capable AI systems could make vulnerability discovery easier for attackers, widening the gap between offensive and defensive security.

Some researchers argue that the same advances can accelerate formal verification, helping teams mathematically prove contract properties and reduce entire classes of vulnerabilities.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
✅ Certora Verifies SPL Token and P-Token Equivalence

Certora formally verified that P-Token, a more compute-efficient reimplementation of Solana's SPL Token, behaves identically to the original token program across shared instructions.

The verification confirms matching acceptance and rejection behavior, no new panics, and byte-for-byte identical account state for all possible inputs.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 DTXT/USDT Pair Drained on BNB Chain

The DTXT/USDT pair was exploited after a flaw in its liquidity-addition detection logic allowed a large token sale to be misclassified, bypassing fee mechanisms.

The attacker used flash-loan-assisted liquidity operations and USDT balance spoofing to drain approximately 35,041 USDT before repaying the flash loan.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🏦 Crypto Neobanks Have More Than One Attack Surface

The $49.5M Infini incident was caused by an unrevoked admin key, not a smart contract bug, highlighting how crypto neobanks inherit risks from both traditional banking and blockchain infrastructure.

Security failures can emerge across custody, governance, card issuance, KYC, APIs, and on-chain systems, making a smart contract audit only one part of the security picture.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Axelar Bug Could Halt Cross-Chain Operations

A disclosed vulnerability in Axelar Network could have allowed an attacker to force the deregistration of Chain Maintainers, dropping validator quorum below required thresholds and halting cross-chain operations across supported EVM chains.

The issue was responsibly disclosed in May 2024, later classified as Critical, and has since been remediated after governance changes disabled the mechanism required to trigger the attack.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Storage Slot Collision Drains 14.41 ETH

A storage slot collision between ATOHook's rewards mapping and Solady's ReentrancyGuard allowed an attacker to inflate reward balances and repeatedly claim funds, resulting in a loss of approximately 14.41 ETH.

The vulnerability caused the "nonReentrant" modifier to overwrite reward accounting data, enabling roughly 200 fraudulent reward claims from the victim contract.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 ZachXBT Links Seized $18.9M to Alleged Crypto Fraud Ring

ZachXBT disputed claims that several detained individuals were simply crypto entrepreneurs, alleging their involvement in social engineering fraud, data extortion, and the $243M Genesis creditor theft, among other incidents.

According to the post, $18.9M in stolen funds was seized by law enforcement in December 2025, with the group allegedly connected to breaches, SIM swaps, and crypto-related fraud targeting victims globally.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛡️ What Separates 100x Hackers From Everyone Else?

According to Immunefi founder Mitchell Amador, a small group of elite researchers disproportionately drives blockchain security by discovering critical vulnerabilities that prevent losses ranging from millions to billions of dollars.

He attributes their impact to deep technical fundamentals, extensive vulnerability knowledge, creativity, persistence, and years of focused research that enable them to uncover exploits others miss.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔍 Inside Gravity Bridge's $5.4M Registry Poisoning Exploit

The attacker poisoned Gravity Bridge's asset registry by registering fake Cosmos assets with crafted denom strings that referenced real Ethereum custody tokens, causing the bridge to associate attacker-controlled assets with legitimate funds.

A missing registry collision check during claim processing allowed the corrupted mappings to be accepted, leading validators to unknowingly authorize withdrawals of approximately $5.4M in real assets.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Syscoin Bridge Validation Flaw Creates 5B Unauthorized SYS

A validation flaw in Syscoin's bridge relay path allowed an attacker to submit a transaction proof that was incorrectly accepted, resulting in the creation of approximately 5B unauthorized SYS on the UTXO side of the bridge.

The bridge has been paused while the team deploys a fix, traces the tainted funds, and coordinates with exchanges and ecosystem partners to block deposits linked to the affected outputs.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Ambient Finance Exploited Through Surplus Collateral Accounting Bug

An attacker used a Balancer flash loan to repeatedly cycle swap and LP operations on Ambient Finance's USDC/ETH pool, exploiting a surplus-collateral accounting flaw to inflate withdrawable balances.

The attack culminated in a "disburseSurplus" call that extracted approximately 83.72 ETH, contributing to total losses of around $110K.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔐 Cygent Adds Dependency Re-Scanning Directly From Chat Platforms

Cygent now allows teams to trigger dependency re-scans from Slack, Discord, and Telegram, returning vulnerability status, affected packages, severity information, and remediation guidance directly within the same conversation thread.

The feature verifies fixes against a project's actual dependency graph, helping teams quickly determine whether vulnerable direct or transitive dependencies remain reachable after an update.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Tether Freezes Wallet Holding 16.65M USDT

Tether froze a wallet holding approximately 16.65M USDT immediately after it received two large transfers totaling around 16.6M USDT.

The wallet is linked to major fund flows involving multiple exchanges and addresses that previously received roughly $100M in withdrawals from BingX.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Humanity Protocol-Linked Wallet Drainer Mints and Dumps 100M Tokens

An ongoing compromise affecting wallets linked to or interacting with Humanity Protocol has resulted in losses exceeding $30M, with the number of drained addresses growing from dozens to hundreds.

The attacker recently minted and sold an additional 100M $H tokens, intensifying sell pressure that has contributed to an approximately 87% decline in the token's price.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Asterix Exploited Through NFT ID Collision Vulnerability

Asterix reportedly lost approximately $40K in an exploit linked to the same high-bit NFT ID collision issue that recently impacted Flooring, where total losses exceeded $900K.

The flaw allows crafted NFT IDs to collide with packed ownership data, breaking accounting and enabling attackers to inflate token balances before selling into liquidity pools to extract WETH.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Update: Humanity Protocol Bridge Compromise Leads to $36M+ Loss

Humanity Protocol disclosed that a compromised employee laptop led to the theft of multiple Gnosis Safe keys, allowing an attacker to seize bridge ProxyAdmin control on both Ethereum and BSC.

The attacker upgraded bridge contracts to malicious implementations, stealing and minting hundreds of millions of H tokens, resulting in losses exceeding $36M.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 TOP Governance Takeover Drains $1.59M From Liquidity Pool

An attacker acquired majority voting power in TOP governance, passed a proposal to mint tokens to themselves, and executed it after surpassing the protocol's governance thresholds.

The newly minted TOP was swapped for WETH through a Balancer pool, draining approximately $1.59M from existing liquidity.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 NovaBox Exploited Through Dividend Accounting Flaw

NovaBox lost approximately 56 ETH after an attacker exploited the order of operations in its ETH deposit and reward distribution logic, allowing a newly added address to receive dividends it had not legitimately earned.

By combining the flaw with a flash loan and immediately withdrawing after the reward misallocation was recorded, the attacker extracted approximately 56.73 ETH in profit.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 MILC Bridge Admin Key Compromise Leads to $161K Loss

A compromised historical admin wallet was used to seize control of MILC Platform's bridge contracts on BNB Chain and Ethereum, granting privileged roles to attacker-controlled addresses and enabling unauthorized withdrawals.

The attacker extracted approximately 97,003 USDT on BNB Chain and 39.21 ETH on Ethereum, for total losses of roughly $161K.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 TesseraDAO Got Drained After Compromised Admin Key Mints 99M TSR

An attacker gained control of TesseraDAO's privileged admin functions, reassigned critical roles, minted 99M TSR tokens, and dumped them for approximately $2.49M, causing the token to collapse by roughly 99%.

The stolen funds were bridged to Ethereum and laundered through Tornado Cash, while the incident exposed the risks of centralized admin control despite the project's public claims of audits, revoked permissions, and multisig governance.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Raydium Exploit Results in $1.3M Loss

According to Specter, Raydium was reportedly exploited for approximately $1.3M, with the attacker draining funds before bridging the stolen assets from Solana to Ethereum.

The attacker later deposited approximately 810 ETH into Tornado Cash and 7 ETH into FixedFloat after initially funding the attack from KuCoin.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Update on the Raydium Incident 

Raydium confirmed that a deprecated Legacy AMM V3 program was exploited for approximately $1.34M after an attacker created a malicious LP token mint and bypassed proportion checks due to insufficient LP mint validation.

The exploit affected five legacy pools and resulted in the theft of approximately 150,177 RAY, 5,603 SOL, and 893,700 USDC. Raydium stated that current programs and users were unaffected and that losses will be covered by the treasury.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛡 DLT Auditor Targets Blockchain Infrastructure Instead of Smart Contracts

DLT Auditor v1 is a free AI-assisted auditing system focused on blockchain infrastructure components such as clients, consensus, execution layers, bridges, mempools, state synchronization, and protocol logic rather than smart contracts alone.

The system uses multiple specialized audit designs and a corpus derived from security-relevant fixes across more than 30 DLT codebases to guide analysis toward historical failure patterns and improve coverage during isolated audit runs.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛡️ OpenZeppelin Outlines Three Security Layers for Institutions Building Onchain

OpenZeppelin argues that institutional blockchain security extends beyond smart contract audits and should be evaluated across three layers: code security, operational security, and compliance posture.

The framework emphasizes audited standards, secure key management, continuous monitoring, operational controls, and ongoing risk assessments as core requirements for financial institutions deploying onchain products.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛡 BlockThreat Launches Community Access Program for Security Researchers

Following support from 115 contributors and The DAO Security Fund during a recent quadratic funding round, BlockThreat announced BlockThreat Community, a free annual sponsored subscription program for students, early-career researchers, solo defenders, and public goods teams.

The initiative will provide access to blockchain threat intelligence, attack trend analysis, DeFi attack vector coverage, security tooling, post-mortems, research, and ecosystem security updates to help strengthen the next generation of defenders.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Suspicious $120M USDT Flow Linked to Cross-Chain Laundering Activity

ZachXBT reported that a wallet which received 120.2M USDT on Tron moved funds through KuCoin, instant exchanges, and cross-chain routes spanning Tron, Bitcoin, and Ethereum.

The laundering activity reportedly drove heavy Monero (XMR) demand, while Tether froze 72M USDT in an address directly linked to the flow.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Shai-Hulud Hades Uses Python-to-Bun Attack Chain

MistEye uncovered a new Shai-Hulud Hades variant on PyPI that abuses .pth files to execute on Python startup, download the Bun runtime if needed, and launch an obfuscated JavaScript payload.

The malware targets GitHub, npm, and cloud credentials, while researchers linked it to earlier Shai-Hulud campaigns through shared infrastructure and RSA keys.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Critical P2Pool Consensus Bug Threatens Mining Payouts

Monero disclosed a critical consensus vulnerability affecting all released versions that could allow an attacker to manipulate mining payouts, potentially redirecting an entire block reward.

A patched release is scheduled for June 13, 2026, and users who fail to update after its publication may remain exposed. The team stated there is currently no evidence of active exploitation.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛡 STRIDE Expands Security Reviews Beyond Smart Contract Audits

STRIDE, developed by Asymmetric Research and the Solana Foundation, is a security framework designed to assess operational, governance, and infrastructure risks that traditional smart contract audits often miss.

The framework evaluates protocols across eight security pillars, assigns maturity scores to individual controls, and publishes assessment results to provide greater transparency into a protocol's overall security posture.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛠 Browser Extension Explains Failed Onchain Transactions

A browser extension explains failed transactions directly on block explorer pages, removing the need to manually inspect traces.

The tool supports over 25,000 EVM error patterns for faster debugging.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛡 ProofOfRep Tracks Security Researcher Experiences With Programs

ProofOfRep is a new reputation platform where security researchers can submit documented reports of unfair or dishonest experiences with bug bounty programs and audit contests.

Submitted reports are manually reviewed to help researchers identify programs with stronger security practices and disclosure processes.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 EasyAuction Division-by-Zero Bug Could Have Permanently Locked Yield DTF Funds

GregoAI had discovered a division-by-zero vulnerability in the Gnosis EasyAuction contract used as a fallback auction mechanism by Reserve Yield DTFs, which could have permanently locked up to $1M in protocol collateral along with bidder funds.

The bug was never exploited, trading was paused as a precaution, and governance proposals are underway to permanently disable the unused batch auction path.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔍 ERC-3643 Makes Compliance a Requirement for Transferability

ERC-3643 uses onchain identity, claim registries, and trusted issuers to enforce transfer restrictions on tokenized securities, requiring buyers to hold approved credentials before a transfer can succeed.

Commonly used for regulated assets such as equity, real estate, and private credit, the standard prioritizes compliance over permissionless liquidity, making transfer requirements a key consideration before investing.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Basis Points Mix-Up Reduced User Refunds by 100x

During an audit, a refund calculation bug was found where a percentage value was passed into logic expecting basis points, causing refunds to be up to 100x smaller than intended when a launch was voided.

Users holding less than 1% of the token supply could also be rounded down to zero, resulting in no refund being received.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛡️ Cygent Generated 116 Tests for an Untested Rust Codebase

A developer used Cygent to analyze an 8,500-line Rust physics simulation with no existing tests, generating implementation-specific invariants and ultimately building a suite of 116 integration tests across nine subsystems.

The resulting tests uncovered previously known and previously undocumented simulation issues, while also documenting additional deferred test cases and creating a long-term regression framework for future development.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Aztec Router Drained of Approximately $2.19M

CertiK detected a suspicious transaction that drained approximately $2.19M from the Aztec Network Router contract on Ethereum.

The funds were moved by the address 0x0f18d8b44a740272f0be4d08338d2b165b7edd17, and the cause of the incident has not yet been disclosed.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 zkSecurity Uncovered Critical Solana ZK Proof Soundness Bug

zkSecurity discovered a critical flaw in Solana's ZK ElGamal Proof Program where a prover-controlled challenge was omitted from the Fiat-Shamir transcript, enabling forged sigma OR proofs.

The bug could have bypassed confidential transfer fee validation in Token-2022. The affected functionality was disabled following disclosure, and no exploitation was detected.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Aztec Connect Exploit Stemmed From Rollup Settlement Boundary Mismatch

Analysis showed the exploit was caused by a mismatch between the transaction set verified by the ZK proof and the transactions processed by L1 settlement logic in RollupProcessorV3.

By placing a real deposit outside the range covered by numRealTxs, the attacker created unbacked balances that bypassed pending deposit accounting and later withdrew them through normal settlement flows, resulting in approximately $2.1M in losses.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Single Signature Enabled $316K USDC Wallet Drain

Following a recent $316K USDC theft flagged by Web3 Antivirus, researchers highlighted how a single malicious signature can be enough to compromise a wallet and authorize asset theft.

The incident serves as a reminder that signatures can be as dangerous as transactions when interacting with smart contracts and dApps.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Thetanuts Legacy Vault Exploited for ~$105K

Thetanuts Finance lost approximately $105.5K USDC after an attacker manipulated the vault's redemption logic by reducing the index token supply to a near-zero level, causing redemptions to return inflated payouts.

The attacker repeatedly cycled mint-and-redeem operations with flash-loaned capital, extracting more underlying assets than were deposited.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛡 Zellic Formally Verified Plonky2 Gates for Lighter

Zellic used formal verification to prove the soundness and completeness of Plonky2 gates used by Lighter, mathematically verifying that circuit constraints correctly enforced their intended computations.

During the process, the team also uncovered an undocumented assumption around carry values in a U32 addition gate, highlighting how formal methods can identify subtle correctness and security issues beyond traditional audits.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Nx Console Supply Chain Attack Led to GitHub Breach

Stolen credentials from the earlier TanStack supply chain attack were used to publish a malicious version of Nx Console on the VS Code Marketplace.

The extension harvested developer credentials and was linked to the compromise of a GitHub employee device, contributing to the exposure of approximately 3,800 repositories.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛡 Certora Co-Founder on Why Formal Verification Matters

Sagiv Mooly, Chief Scientist and Co-founder of Certora, explained why crypto systems are especially attractive targets for attackers.

He discussed how formal verification helps protocols mathematically prove correctness and reduce exploitable vulnerabilities.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛡 Sherlock AI Reported Multiple Validated Findings Across Recent Reviews

Sherlock AI was adopted for internal security reviews by two major protocols and recently identified a confirmed High-severity issue in a cross-chain lending protocol following a private audit.

The platform also reported a validated Critical finding and multiple validated Medium-severity issues during a large L1 security review.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛡️ OpenZeppelin Move Contracts for Sui Released v1.3

OpenZeppelin released v1.3 of its Move Contracts library for Sui, expanding the set of audited building blocks available to developers.

The update introduces rate limiting, role-based access control, and DeFi math primitives for AMM swaps and bonding curves.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 DIP Token Double-Transfer Bug Drained ~$111K USDC

An attacker stole approximately $111,097.6 USDC from a PancakeSwap DIP liquidity pool by exploiting a bug in the DIP token's "_transfer()" function, where a missing return statement caused transfers involving the PancakeSwap Router to execute twice.

By repeatedly triggering double DIP transfers through "skim(router)" and then calling "sync()" to distort the pool's reserves, the attacker manipulated the AMM price and drained funds from the pool.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Supply Chain Attack Affected 140+ Mastra Packages

A coordinated npm supply chain attack introduced a malicious dependency into more than 140 Mastra packages, allowing attacker-controlled code to execute automatically during package installation.

The malware was capable of collecting system and browser data, identifying cryptocurrency wallet extensions, establishing persistence, and exfiltrating sensitive information from affected environments.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Four Major Incidents Resulted in ~$5.98M in Losses

Four notable exploits were reported across Ethereum and Solana during the week of June 8–14, resulting in approximately $5.98M in losses.

The largest incidents affected Aztec and Raydium, which together accounted for roughly $3.5M of the total losses.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛡 True Markets Converter Accepted Arbitrary Market Contracts

The TokenConverter trusted any user-supplied market address and used its responses to determine token approvals and redemption logic without verifying that the market was legitimate.

An attacker could deploy a fake market contract, return arbitrary values for the winning token and market outcome, receive approval over the converter's balance, and transfer all held tokens through a malicious redemption call.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Aztec Hit by Another ~$2M Exploit Days After Previous Incident

Approximately 1,158 ETH (~$2M) was drained from Aztec's Private Rollup Bridge through a successful escapeHatch execution, marking a separate incident from the recent $2.15M Aztec Connect exploit.

The contract accepted the submitted proof package and released the funds without reverting, with early analysis pointing toward a potential issue in proof validation or state binding rather than a conventional smart contract bug.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Little Boy Plus Exploited for ~$367K Through Reserve Manipulation

The attacker inflated the USDT reserves observed by the protocol by transferring funds directly into the LBP/USDT pair and calling mint, causing the hashrate emission logic to overestimate LP value and mint roughly 10.7M hLBP.

The inflated emissions triggered additional LBP rewards, allowing the attacker to dump approximately 141K LBP for profit before repaying flash loans and exiting with roughly 377K USDT.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛡️ ERC-7540 Adds Asynchronous Flows to Tokenized Vaults

An implementation of ERC-7540 has been merged with contributions from Centrifuge and Superform, extending ERC-4626 vaults with request-and-claim flows for deposits and withdrawals.

The standard is designed for tokenized treasuries, private credit, and regulated funds where settlement depends on offchain processes such as compliance checks or wire transfers before shares can be issued or redeemed.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔍 New Analysis Examines the Math Behind the Cetus Exploit

A new article by gneiss2meetU explores how the ~$223M Cetus exploit stemmed from mathematical assumptions rather than an access control failure.

The piece focuses on arithmetic, precision loss, rounding behavior, and custom math implementations in Move-based protocols, where vulnerabilities can emerge beyond the language's built-in safety guarantees.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Microsoft Warns of New Crypto Clipper Malware Campaign

Microsoft Security reported a crypto clipper malware campaign active since February 2026 that targets cryptocurrency users by monitoring clipboard activity.

The malware can steal seed phrases and private keys, capture screenshots, and replace copied wallet addresses with attacker-controlled addresses.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛡 AI Is Making Security Engineers More Effective, Not Replacing Them

AI is already helping security teams find real vulnerabilities, navigate large codebases, generate tests, compare implementations, and accelerate threat modelling, bug hunting, and review workflows.

The article argues that the strongest security model today is AI-assisted engineers, where AI increases speed and coverage while humans remain responsible for protocol understanding, adversarial reasoning, exploit validation, and final security judgement.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 mySwap CL Protocol Exploited for ~$300K

The mySwap CL protocol was exploited at approximately 7:15 AM UTC, resulting in the theft of roughly $300K from its liquidity pools and the near-complete depletion of the protocol's remaining liquidity.

The attacker has since bridged the stolen assets and used Railgun to obscure fund movements, while the protocol's interface remains closed to new liquidity following more than six months of inactivity.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 ~$4.67M Drained From Axelar Assets Bridged to Secret Network

Approximately $4.67M in assets bridged from Axelar to Secret Network over IBC were stolen in an incident linked to the Secret-side ICS-20 contract handling the Cosmos IBC connection between the two networks.

In response, Axelar's emergency committee disabled the Secret and Secret-SNIP connections. According to the team, the issue is isolated to Axelar-bridged assets on Secret, while Axelar’s core protocol, other IBC connections, and other integrations remain unaffected.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Secret Network CW20-ICS20 Exploit Root Cause

A modified CW20-ICS20 bridge contract on Secret minted unbacked saTokens by trusting denom names without verifying the IBC source channel.

The attacker opened a fake channel, forged deposits, minted fake assets, then redeemed them through the real Axelar route to drain ~$4.67M in escrowed funds.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Researchers Investigating Weak Seed Generation in Multi-Chain Mobile Wallet

Researchers said they are investigating a wallet that may have used weak seed generation since 2018, affecting support for EVM, Bitcoin, and other chains.

Current evidence points to a JavaScript/React Native/Expo mobile wallet. The wallet does not appear to be widely used, but affected users could still be at risk.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Namada MASP Reportedly Drained While Indexer Still Showed Funds

The reported incident claims Namada’s shielded pool was drained of roughly $600K in liquid IBC assets, while the indexer continued showing balances that live RPC queries returned as zero.

ATOM, USDC, OSMO, TIA, and NYM were reportedly swept, while staked assets were left untouched. The discrepancy appears to come from stale indexer data rather than the live chain state.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 OLPC/LABUBU Pool Exploit on BNB Chain Led to ~$1.1M Loss

PeckShield reported that an exploit affecting an OLPC/LABUBU pool on BNB Chain resulted in roughly $1.1M in losses, with the attacker later bridging funds to Ethereum and depositing 633.4 ETH into Tornado Cash.

The issue was attributed to the token contract itself, not to PancakeSwap’s smart contracts.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 JaredFromSubway MEV Bot Drained for $7.5M via Malicious Approval Routes

Blockaid reported that attacker-controlled contracts fed fake MEV opportunities to JaredFromSubway’s automated execution system, causing the bot to approve malicious helper contracts as spenders for WETH, USDC, and USDT.

In earlier transactions those approvals were consumed during execution, but later crafted routes left the allowances standing. The attacker then used transferFrom through a sweep contract to drain roughly $7.5M from the bot.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Front-End Attack Reported on Gitcoin Subdomain

Blockaid reported a front-end compromise affecting "files[.]gitcoin[.]co", where the site was found serving Eleven drainer code.

Users were advised not to interact with the site while the incident is being investigated and remediated.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 ZachXBT Says Frozen 5.73 BTC Was Traced to Social Engineering Theft Cluster

ZachXBT said a user who complained about 5.73 BTC frozen at Changelly was linked to funds traced back to social engineering thefts targeting Americans through exchanges and Bitcoin ATMs, with the broader cluster allegedly taking over $1M from victims since 2025.

According to Zach, the sender’s explanation for the funds changed multiple times, and additional clues from email screenshots pointed to a wider group. He said he suspects the account was being used as a mule for another operator.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛡️ Immunefi Launches IronScore for Protocol Security Intelligence

Immunefi has launched IronScore, a free scoring system that rates the security posture of crypto protocols from 0 to 100 using verified, publicly traceable security data.

It is built for researchers, protocols, and token holders: helping researchers identify serious programs, protocols benchmark their security posture, and users inspect how much of a wallet’s value depends on weakly secured protocols.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Taiko Has Been Exploited For ~1.7M

Early analysis suggests the reported exploit may have originated from a Raiko SGX enclave signing key that was exposed on GitHub, potentially breaking the prover trust model behind Taiko’s proof verification flow.

DeFi losses dropped 50% from H1 2025 to H1 2026 ($1.86B vs $935.3M), but incidents nearly tripled and average severity fell from $49M to $10.75M per hack, pointing to a shift from rare, massive exploits to a higher volume of smaller ones.

text:
🔮 Bonzo Finance Drained for $9.05M via Oracle Signature Bypass

Supra's oracle verifier accepted a zero-byte signature because the committee's public key was never registered on-chain, letting the attacker spoof SAUCE collateral price and drain 6.63M USDC and 34.5M WHBAR from Bonzo Finance on Hedera.

Stolen funds were bridged via Stargate to Arbitrum, Base, and Ethereum before flowing into Tornado Cash, while a self-reported whitehat scooped ~$1M separately and claims to be returning it.

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔮 How $3 of Collateral Became a $9M Payday on Bonzo Finance

The attacker pushed a price update to Supra's oracle with a zeroed BLS signature, which passed verification because both the signature and the unregistered committee public key resolved to the identity point, making the pairing check trivially true.

With SAUCE collateral priced at 12 orders of magnitude above reality, the attacker borrowed 6.63M USDC and 34.5M WHBAR in the next transaction, no flash loan needed, then bridged ~$5.25M to Ethereum via LayerZero.

🔑 Critical Flaw in Zilliqa Ledger App Exposes Private Keys From On-Chain Data

A nonce-generation bug in the Zilliqa Ledger app has been present since 2019, causing Schnorr signatures to use predictably biased nonces with the top 64 bits fixed at zero, allowing private key recovery from just 5+ on-chain signatures using lattice reduction.

Affected keys cannot be secured by simply moving funds, as attackers can front-run transfers using the already-derived private key. Users should await official Zilliqa guidance before taking any action.

NIST's post-quantum standards offer replacements, but migration is costly and complex, and already-exposed keys can only be protected by moving funds before quantum computers arrive.

Native USDC uses 18 decimals while ERC-20 USDC uses 6, and a CallFrom precompile preserves the original caller across contracts, both easy to miss when porting Ethereum code untested on Arc.

text:
🔓 Tectonic's $120.4M Exploit Traced to Verifiable Exchange Rate Flaw

Formal verification found that direct TONIC transfers to the tTONIC market could inflate its exchange rate without going through the intended mint path.

The attacker combined this with DEX price manipulation on thin TONIC liquidity to inflate collateral value from both angles before borrowing across nine markets.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🏆 Audit Competitions Are Shrinking, and Quantus Shows Why

Public audit competitions fell from 89 in Q4 2024 to just 11 by Q2 2026, with Code4rena winding down entirely.

Quantus's $20K competition drew 66 valid findings from 98 researchers, but one high-severity bug alone got 25 duplicate reports, exposing how reward splitting breaks down when everyone races to report the same thing.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🏠 QuillAudits Finds Missing Access Control in Tokenized Real Estate Protocol

Sellers approve a launchpad contract to move their NFT property shares for listing, and the core property contract trusts that launchpad completely.

The catch: an internal transfer function meant only for the listing flow had no access control, so any user could call it directly and walk off with a seller's shares for free.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔐 Multisig Security Isn't Just About Signature Thresholds

Ronin, Harmony Horizon, and Orbit Chain lost a combined $805M despite requiring 5 of 9, 2 of 5, and 7 of 10 signatures, because the same team or company controlled enough of those keys to hit quorum.

The fix isn't a higher threshold, it's adding signers who are actually independent and who verify the deployed code matches what they reviewed before signing.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
📊 Weekly Roundup: ~$11.3M Lost Across Two Web3 Incidents

A multicall router let a nested self-call inherit the router's own trusted identity, bypassing a Safe module's caller check and enabling a ~$7.8M withdrawal.

Nostra's Starknet money market accepted an oracle price from just one contributing source below its intended minimum, letting a manipulated thin-pool quote value collateral high enough to borrow ~$3.5M against it.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Payy Rollup Drained of ~$1.83M USDC

Specter flagged the exploit on Payy's rollup, with the attacker converting the stolen funds into 683.38 ETH.

The ETH was then split mainly across three wallets, a pattern typically used to complicate tracing before further movement or laundering.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Meter Ongoing Exploit: ~$2.3M in Unbacked Wrapped MTRG Minted

Blockaid flagged an active exploit on Meter's BNB Chain deployment, where an attacker used Meter Passport to mint wrapped MTRG without backing it with real collateral.

Roughly $2.3M in unbacked tokens has been minted across two transactions so far, with part of it already sold on PancakeSwap as the attack continues.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Duelbits Confirms ~$7M Hack, Platform Taken Offline

Hot wallets on Ethereum, BSC, Tron and Bitcoin saw ~$4.9M in outflows to newly created addresses, moving 836 ETH, 1.62M USDT, 97K USDC, 209 BNB, 192K TRX and 8.1 BTC.

Co-founder Joe confirmed the ~$7M hack and said Duelbits will stay offline until the investigation concludes, with user funds reported safe and hot wallets to be re-topped before relaunch.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Bitget Hot & Cold Wallets Hacked: Over $170M Drained

An exploiter has swapped funds from three hot wallets and one cold wallet to ETH, with over $174M sent to a single address across multiple chains within the hour.

The affected wallets still hold roughly $530M, and Bitget appears to be actively moving remaining funds to other wallets to limit further losses.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔗 Bitget Hack Linked to Lazarus Group

Specter traced the stolen XRP from the Bitget hack back to the same funds taken in July's $24M AFX hack, which was attributed to TraderTraitor.

The bridging pattern links both incidents to the Lazarus Group.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🖼️ Whitehat Rescues 23,155 NFTs After LimitBreak Payment Processor Exploit

An exploit in Payment Processor V2 let an attacker steal Meebits, Otherdeeds and other NFTs starting at 9AM EST, with LimitBreak pausing the affected V3 contract once alerted, though the unpausable V2 required a whitehat rescue instead.

The operation recovered over 23,155 NFTs worth north of $5.7M, though 660 WETH exposed by a related exploit path couldn't be saved in time.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
📢 Bitget Confirms $387.5M Lost, Launches Recovery Bounty

Bitget has raised its confirmed loss from the September 24 incident to approximately $387.5M, after including affected assets on Zcash and TRON.

Bitget has fixed the vulnerability and confirmed the incident is contained, with a bounty of 5% on frozen or recovered funds now live and withdrawals expected back by September 26, 4:00AM UTC.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
⚖️ Kelp Sues LayerZero Over rsETH Bridge Exploit

Kelp has filed a lawsuit against LayerZero and co-founder Bryan Pellegrino, alleging the earlier rsETH bridge exploit stemmed from undisclosed weaknesses and a security failure on LayerZero's own infrastructure.

The complaint claims LayerZero reviewed and endorsed the deployment in writing before publicly shifting blame, while Kelp says it has since migrated the bridge to a more secure standard.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🧬 DAOstack's Genesis Alpha Pilot DAO Drained via Governance Takeover

A shared controller let anyone register a fake org pointing at another DAO's real reputation token, since it never checked if that reputation was already governed elsewhere.

The attacker minted majority voting power, self-approved a full-permission scheme on the real DAO, then drained its ~4.02 ETH treasury.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛠️ Solidity-Auditor V4 Released Open Source Under MIT License

The tool now reaches up to 85% recall on High severity findings from multi-week audit contests held last year, run from a single command.

It replicates functionality that previously cost protocols tens of thousands of dollars, now available for free from the PAG team.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🎭 TraderTraitor Targets Non-Crypto Firm With Weaponized Terraform Files

The DPRK-linked group behind April's ~$292M LayerZero/KelpDAO breach compromised an India-based IT firm via fake job interviews, using malicious Terraform files to deploy macOS backdoors.

The backdoors steal credentials and cloud/source-control access, suggesting the group now targets any org whose developers can reach valuable infrastructure.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🎭 Fake GIWA Chain Nets Scammers $2M+ in Hours

An attacker fabricated an entire fake GIWA chain, RPC and bridge included, convincing enough that DYORSwap listed it as legitimate.

The scam pulled in over $2M in hours before being caught.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🕵️ Fake GIWA Bridge Timeline: From Setup to $2M+ Drain

Signers were funded via ChangeHero on Sep 26, with the fake bridge going live 11 hours later and pulling in 767 ETH from 1,333 wallets.

Thirteen hours later, the Safe swapped its portal code and drained 766 ETH in one tx, with 177 ETH already through Tornado and 589 ETH still in four wallets.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🎯 Bug Bounty Hunter Breaks Down His AI-Assisted Methodology

Security researcher 0xvivekd, who earned nearly $1.4M in bug bounties this year, shares how he got started and the process behind his hunts in a new video.

The breakdown covers how he uses AI to find real vulnerabilities and where he sees bug bounties heading next.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🕵️ Officer's Notes Launches OSINT & On-Chain Investigation Service

Longtime investigator Officer's Notes has launched a new website offering background checks and on-chain investigation services alongside partners.

The site is live for anyone who may need OSINT or blockchain tracing support.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🧮 Nostra Oracle Averaged a $0.006 Quote With a $99 Quote

With only two price sources reporting, the oracle blended a clean NSTR price with a manipulated one, inflating collateral value roughly 8,306x.

That let about $421 of real NSTR support ~$3.5M in borrowing, a loan Pragma says a three-source minimum would have blocked.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🕵️ ZachXBT: Chinese Launderers Moving Bitget Exploit Funds for DPRK

Chinese illicit actors are laundering proceeds from the $387M Bitget exploit for the alleged DPRK attackers, openly asking for support in public Discord and Telegram channels.

One alias also laundered funds from the $292M Kelp DAO exploit, and the funds are being chain-hopped via bridges into mixers like Wasabi.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔬 CertiK Formally Verifies zkWasm, Proving Soundness of a Leading zkVM

Using the Coq proof assistant, CertiK translated zkWasm's Halo2 circuits into machine-checked proofs showing that every accepted execution trace is a valid Wasm execution and that a malicious prover cannot forge a proof for an incorrect one.

The verification covers arithmetic, memory, control-flow and call instructions plus supporting tables, and has been accepted at ACM CCS 2026.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
📉 Balancer Lead Proposes Winddown After V3 Revenue Bet Falls Short

Balancer cut its team from 25 to 12.5 FTEs and routed fees to the DAO under an April restructuring, but v3 revenue never grew enough to replace v2's.

Marcus cites lasting partner hesitancy since November's exploit and is now proposing a winddown rather than spend treasury on a path already tried.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🥪 Relay API Leak Let Searchers Sandwich ~5,600 Users for $136K

Pending trade routes exposed through Relay's API let MEV searchers infer trades and front-run them before execution, from Sep 12 to 26, with most activity concentrated in the last few days.

Relay is paying a $50K bounty to the researcher who reported it and compensating all affected users automatically, totaling roughly $312K.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Dutch Police Arrest "Umbreon" Over ShinyHunters Links

Authorities arrested 23-year-old Pepijn van der Stap, known online as Umbreon, over suspected ties to ShinyHunters.

The previously convicted hacker, who called himself reformed since his 2025 release, is now linked to recent extortion campaigns including the Odido breach.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
📊 SEAL Weekly: 67 Incidents, Fake Support Scams Lead at $8M

SEAL handled 67 incidents from Sep 22-29, with fake support callers topping losses at $8M by tricking victims into granting access to Gmail and CEX accounts.

Seed compromises added $6.74M and protocol/infrastructure exploits another $3.56M plus 703 ETH, while the team published 3,293 phishing domains and 193 flagged wallets.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔑 Stolen Keys & Phishing Drive Two-Thirds of Hack Losses

Dedaub classified 135 Rekt-reported incidents from Jan 2024 to Aug 2026, totaling $4.9B in losses.

Stolen keys, phishing, malware and privileged access made up 32.6% of incidents but 66.9% of the money lost.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔁 MUSystem Loses ~$36.9K to Deposit Bonus Double-Count

The deposit function counted a first-deposit bonus in both the immediate ETH refund and the user's MUS allocation, while withdraw allowed same-transaction redemption without capping the ETH returned to what was actually deposited.

Sixteen fresh addresses repeated the cycle to drain ETH from the contract.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🌲 ZachXBT: DPRK Attackers Shielding Stolen ZEC via Ironwood

The alleged Bitget attackers have begun shielding ~2.7K ZEC (~$3.8M) of the 18.9K ZEC (~$28.3M) stolen, using the Ironwood privacy pool.

The move undercuts the common claim that threat actors avoid ZEC.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🍰 SKYDAO/USDT Pool Drained of ~183K USDT via Premature Sync

SKYDAO's sell flow burned tax tokens and synced pool reserves before crediting the seller's net tokens, briefly recording near-zero reserves.

A flash-loan attacker swapped directly against that gap, netting 59,914 USDT after repaying the loan.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
💰 Ostium Launches Recovery Portal After $23.75M Attack

After the July 15th attack drained ~$23.75M from its Liquidity Pool, Ostium's new Recovery Portal offers 90.59% of affected wallets full recovery.

Small losses can be claimed immediately, larger ones choose between a capped payout or pro-rata recovery over time.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔑 Onchain Sleuth Traces MetaMask Validator Fee Hijack

An attacker rerouted block rewards from 18 MetaMask validators to a Tornado-funded address, netting only ~0.36 ETH.

~17K validators (~523K ETH) exited as a precaution, but 821 potentially affected ones haven't, and the attacker may be able to trigger slashing.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
📊 September Hits Record $766.4M in Losses for 2026

Combining exploits and phishing, CertiK has confirmed approximately $766.4M lost across September.

The month recorded both the highest total losses and the highest number of incidents seen so far in 2026.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 ZachXBT: Near Intents Possibly Exploited for $3.8M+

Near Intents' BSC hot wallet saw multiple irregular outflows before processing stopped, with the site status page now showing an ongoing incident affecting multiple EVM chains.

The stolen funds were immediately moved to KuCoin and bridged to Bitcoin.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔓 FlashLoopAdapter Safe Module Drained for $305K

A Safe module for Aave v3 leveraged loops trusted any contract that answered isModuleEnabled() as true, including a fake "Safe" built by the attacker.

Posing as both the swap router and flash loan provider, the attacker used the enabled module to drain weETH collateral from two Safes sharing the same owner.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
📊 PeckShield: September Losses Hit $766.49M, Up 462% MoM

September saw 55 major hacks totaling $766.49M, a roughly 462% jump from August's $136.3M.

Bitget (~$387M) and Liquid Network (~$320M, with $285M returned) now rank as the year's two largest thefts, surpassing the earlier Drift and Kelp DAO/LayerZero exploits.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🕵🏽 Bitget Hacker Loses ~$700K to Wrong-Chain Laundering Mistake

The attacker's script sent ~267K USDC to a Chainflip channel that only exists on Arbitrum while on Ethereum, an address since blacklisted by Circle.

A second mix-up sent ~160 ETH (~$430K) to an Ethereum-only channel while on Arbitrum, leaving it stuck with no way to sweep it.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🤖 Cantina Releases Apex-Flash-1, Open-Weights Security Research Model

Cantina has released apex-flash-1, its first open-weights model for security research, post-trained on real vulnerabilities it found and got paid for.

An abliterated variant is also available for researchers wanting fewer refusals in authorized workflows.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
💸 Near Intents Hacker Returns Full $3.8M

The attacker behind Thursday's $3.8M Near Intents exploit returned the funds in full, according to GM Alex Shevchenko, about 15 hours after the team identified them and gave a 48-hour deadline.

Shevchenko said the team is closing its investigation and urged hackers to use bug bounties instead of disrupting services.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔍 Certora: Audits, Fuzzing and Formal Verification Each Miss Different Bugs

Of 245 incidents from Jan 2025 to July 2026, 147 hit audited platforms, which accounted for 88% of the $3.63B stolen.

Certora argues the three methods cover different gaps, citing a Maker bug that took a fuzzer 13 hours to find and its Prover 23 seconds.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔦 Lighthouse Releases v8.2.3 Security Fix and v8.3.0-rc.0

Lighthouse v8.2.3 is a medium-priority mainnet release that patches security vulnerabilities.

The v8.3.0-rc.0 release adds Glamsterdam support for Sepolia ahead of its October 6 activation, with v8.3.0 stable planned for next week.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🪝 GoldPesa Uniswap v4 Hook Drained for $114K

The hook's rebalance collected the PositionManager's full net credit, shared by every caller in the same unlock.

The attacker left ~115K USDC of unpaid debt there, so the hook's burn proceeds were netted against it and the hook effectively paid for the attacker's position.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔄 MALT Pool Drained of ~$72K via Hook-Funded Liquidity

The swap called a rebalance hook that deposited treasury DAI into the pool before output was sent.

The invariant check counted that DAI as the caller's input, letting an attacker with negligible input withdraw excess MALT.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Unnamed Base Vault Exploit Passes $6M and Is Still Ongoing

Blockaid detected an attacker adding a brand-new contract to the vault's whitelist, then borrowing aBaswstETH and sending the aTokens to their own contract.

The drain started at ~$2.02M across four transactions and has now grown past $6M.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔓 Critical Better Auth Bypass Lets Attackers Take Over Any Account

Rick de Jager, using V12, found a CVSS 9.1 flaw in Better Auth, which sees over 9.5M weekly downloads. Magic Link tokens and OAuth state shared one verification table with no prefix separating them.

An attacker could start a social sign-in with the victim's email and submit the OAuth state to the magic link endpoint to get the victim's session. It's fixed in 1.7.7.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🤖 Immunefi Opens Studio Cohort to AI Security Agent Builders

Immunefi is forming a specialized cohort of AI security agent builders inside Studio, offering early access to new features and a role in shaping the product.

It is also expanding its AI Agent Benchmarking system, with interested teams already being added to the upcoming list.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
📚 23K Audit Findings With PoCs and Fixes Released for Free

A free collection of 23,000 audit findings, each with a proof of concept and fix is available to web3 security researchers.

The dataset was created by Zaevlad.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
📊 CertiK: September Ranks 2nd Worst Month in 3 Years

September trailed only February 2025's Bybit incident, and Q3 losses reached ~$1.27B, up 54.4% from Q2 across 249 incidents.

Year-to-date losses of ~$2.69B have already passed all of 2023, and the current trajectory would surpass 2025's ~$3.4B.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🖍 ExVul Decompiler Adds Screenshot and Annotation Support

Users can now capture code snippets, mark them with red notes, arrows and boxes, and download the image to share findings.

The update makes contract analysis easier to follow and present.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🕵️ ZachXBT Infiltrates Syndicate Laundering $1B+ for Lazarus

Posing as a client, ZachXBT fronted $349.7K and lost 5% per order to gain a launderer's trust, who then exposed $12M+ of Bybit funds moving across chains.

The intel led to a 442K USDT Tether freeze and tied the group to a sanctioned Huione Guarantee wallet, with findings shared with law enforcement.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🪝 Uniswap v4 Hook on Base Pays Attacker's $115K Debt

An attacker left $115K of debt on Uniswap's shared PositionManager, then triggered the hook's rebalance in the same transaction.

The hook's own liquidity ended up covering the bill.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Set Protocol Loses ~5.08 ETH to Fee Rounding Bug

A fee update rounded the per-share unit up from 4,927 to 4,928 even though no fee was minted.

The attacker issued before the update and redeemed after it, using Uniswap v4 flash accounting to scale the extraction.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🤖 Dormant MakerDAO Keeper Bot Drained of ~$538K

A 2020 liquidation keeper had won four ETH-A auctions but never claimed them, leaving 200 WETH locked in the Flipper.

Its drain routine had no access control, so a Tornado-funded address called it and withdrew everything. MakerDAO core contracts behaved as designed.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🌊 Immunefi Warns AI Is Flooding Vulnerability Intake Systems

Immunefi reports 24,418 submissions in 2025, up 135%, while NIST expects to fully analyze only 15% to 20% of incoming CVEs.

Open source maintainers are already buckling, with cURL closing its bug bounty over AI-generated reports.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
💸 Researcher Pays $95 to Learn Immunefi Studio Missed a Duplicate

A researcher paid $20 for an Immunefi Studio review that marked his High severity report "Ready," then paid $75 to submit it.

It was closed as a duplicate 15 minutes later of a report filed 9 days earlier, a risk Studio is advertised to check.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔑 QuillAudit Finds Open Signing Oracle Behind a Payment Protocol's Multisig

The protocol's signing service held a hot key but accepted unauthenticated requests, letting any network peer sign with any named key over a multi-million dollar pool.

The review also found no spending caps on that key and a retry cache that could duplicate payments.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🎮 The Red Village Loses $80.7K via Public Router Call

A public router function let anyone call any service, so the attacker used its upgrade role to swap in a backdoored contract.

The backdoor drained WETH from ~299 approved player wallets, and the exploiter has since received an onchain bounty offer.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🕵️ Frogman Attacker Nets ~$2.4M, Funds Traced to Privacy Cash and XMR

AMLBot traced ~13,241 SOL (~$1.54M) into Privacy Cash and ~$815K through Hyperliquid, where it was converted to XMR.

Smaller amounts reached KuCoin (160 SOL, ~$18.6K) and an unidentified service (~80 SOL, ~$9.3K).

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🗳 Disguised HAI Proposal Tries to Hand Attacker 34% of Voting Power

A proposal labeled "Quarterly Treasury Maintenance" hid an action delegating the DAO treasury's 328K KITE (~34% of supply) to the proposer.

That would far exceed the 1% quorum, putting ~$927K at risk, though no funds have moved yet.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔁 X7 Finance Loses ~6.78 ETH to Reward Accounting Bug

The reward claim added unaccounted ETH to total rewards on every call but only updated its balance checkpoint when something was claimable.

Calling it with no claims repeated the addition and inflated the per-token reward, and the attacker donated ETH to amplify it before draining funds.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔑 79th Vault Drained of $12.5M via Compromised Operator Key

An operator-only token function let the key pull 2.01M 79AU out of the PancakeSwap pair in seven transfers, and the attacker sold them back through ~95 swaps.

The pair's USDT reserve fell from $15.2M to $3.9M. The attacker cashed out 16,249 BNB, and the operator key later funded their address, so it was either compromised or an insider.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🛡 Justin Drake Urges "Bunker Mode" Migration to Hash-Protected Addresses

Drake recommends holders move funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction, warning AI-driven math breakthroughs could break ECDSA within months.

He also urges oracles and L2 councils to rotate keys or add hash-based signatures like SPHINCS.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🏦 BitBay Vault Loses ~$14K to Zero-Liquidity Withdrawal Bug

The vault's withdraw logic paid out its entire token balance when liquidity was zero, instead of the user's proportional share.

The attacker triggered that state with a reposition, then redeemed one minimal share unit to drain ~14,838 DAI.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔢 EtherVista Pair Drained of ~$18.6K via Overflow in Invariant Check

The pair's swap check multiplied two uint112 reserves, which overflowed and let the invariant pass even as the real reserve product fell.

The attacker registered their own contract as the authorized router and ran two crafted swaps to drain WETH and VISTA.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🚨 Specter Traces $86M+ Stolen From Ledger Users Across Chains

Specter traced inflows from hundreds of victim wallets on Ethereum, TRON and Bitcoin following reports of wallet-draining by Ledger users on X and Reddit.

The theft addresses show total losses of $86M+, and the cause hasn't been confirmed.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔖 Bookmark Phishing Targets FOMO Users With Malicious JavaScript

A fake CAPTCHA page tells users to drag JavaScript into their browser bookmarks.

Clicking that bookmark 2-3 times lets attackers hijack a logged-in FOMO account and steal its crypto assets.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🌉 $3.55M in Unclaimed Bridge Funds Moved via EIP-7702 Delegations

Claims were submitted from a Tornado-funded address through EIP-7702 delegations on the owner's account, days after a researcher warned the owner the funds were still claimable.

Onchain data confirms the authorizations were valid, but not whether the owner signed them knowingly, was tricked, or had their key compromised.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
✈️ Telegram Desktop Flaw Lets One Clicked Link Take Over Accounts

Researcher BeakSec found that the link injects hidden commands that make the app send the victim's session files to the attacker.

Telegram allegedly fixed the issue, tracked as CVE - 2026 - 107181, in version 7.2.9.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔌 Ledger Drain Traced to Possibly Tampered Devices From an Authorized Reseller

A researcher found a hidden LTE modem board inside a Ledger bought from cryptobilis, an authorized Malaysian reseller sold to a new owner this spring, and ~$91M was swept about 22 hours after the teardown went public.

Nobody has officially tied the new owner to the bugged devices, and Ledger hasn't confirmed the cause, though it asked the reseller to pause sales.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🔥 USDT Contract Lets Tether Burn Blacklisted Balances and Reissue Them

Tether's owner multisig can zero out a blacklisted address's balance and cut total supply by that amount, with no way to reverse it.

The same amount can then be minted to another address, a process the DOJ described in a March 2025 Massachusetts forfeiture case over ~$9M in USDT.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🧬 Veria's AI Finds XRP Ledger Bug That Could Mint 18 Trillion XRP

Veria says its AI agent chained two low-severity bugs in rippled, some of it code from 2015 and 2017, to let an unauthenticated attacker mint 184x the total supply in one transaction, putting the $94B market cap at risk.

Ripple fixed it within three days, skipping the usual amendment vote for the first time in over ten years, and found no evidence of exploitation. Veria received the $250K maximum bounty.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
🕳 Rekt: NEAR Intents' $3.87M Drain Returned, Root Cause Still Unexplained

A bridge vault paid out 3,865,000 USDT against a 10 USDT deposit, with ~$822K of the loot routed through NEAR Intents' own service mid-drain.

The funds came back in full, but the promised report never did and the investigation was closed.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:
📊 BlockSec Roundup: ~$418M Lost Across 8 Incidents in Two Weeks

BlockSec's report for Sep 21 to Oct 4 counts eight incidents totaling about $418.4M across Ethereum, BNB Chain, Solana, Bitcoin, TRON, XRP Ledger and others.

The deep dives cover Bitget's $387.5M loss from a third-party security product vulnerability and NEAR Intents' $3.87M refund validation flaw.

🔗 Details

author: Defendor — DeFi Security
text:

He adds that MPC signers did not independently verify transactions, so one breached node broke the scheme.

Names, usernames, password hashes, and valid authentication tokens of all users were exposed.

The withdraw logic accepted negative fees, so the attacker set the fee to the withdrawal amount with a minus sign, and the system deducted nothing while still sending the full amount.

Fixing a wrong architectural assumption after deployment means rewriting contracts, migrating users, and auditing everything again.

Their architecture assessments cover new integrations, deployment on unfamiliar networks, and role-based risks such as who can pause or upgrade.

Attackers accessed its legacy B2C card system on November 3, exposing some customer information, though customer funds and the enterprise card platform were unaffected.

Gnosis Pay replaced the compromised credentials, made 3D Secure mandatory for online payments, and will retire the legacy system on December 20.

Accounts created with Google or Apple login may be affected, while wallets made with a recovery phrase or hardware wallet are not.

A malicious peer could also trigger sync restarts, dropping a test node from height 120 to 6, and fixes have shipped.

Total losses for 2026 now stand near $9.2B, the highest on record.

text:
🔍 ERC-7730 Clear Signing Makes Intent Legible, Not Honest

The standard turns raw calldata into a readable prompt, but the descriptor itself can be stale, spoofable, or adversarial.

Key risks include spoofed token names, stale descriptors after upgrades, and hidden execution fields.

He says Canada is a bottom-three jurisdiction globally because ineffective laws leave it open to abuse.

text:

The attacker used a valid signature to set an EIP-7702 delegation, a standing instruction that let funds move without further signatures.

The guide says to limit signing access, treat delegation as an admin privilege, cap damage if signing is compromised, and monitor authority changes.

Unauthenticated attackers can execute arbitrary code through crafted Flight payloads that carry multiple typed arrays and attacker-controlled values.

Affected React versions include 19.0.0 to 19.3.0, and users should upgrade to 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9, or 19.3.1, or to Next.js 16.4.1 or 15.5.28.

The attacker reversed the swap and kept the spread, since the slippage floor reused the same manipulable quote.
